# Hypercolor 0.8.0

## Studio

Studio now uses one tab per zone, a device pane, and drag and drop with menu equivalents. New placements use the rig layout, and Fit brings the zone's devices into view. Layout edits save as they happen and share one undo history with device moves and zone operations.

Scene selection and zone tabs are consistent across pages. The Studio documentation follows the new workflow.

## Scene writes

Scene snapshots pair their contents with the revision they describe. Conditional writes can name both the daemon run and revision, and structural scene-tree mutations accept idempotency keys for retrying a request without applying it twice.

Queued placement edits preserve fields changed by another client when the local edit did not touch them. A create-and-fill operation retains its undo receipt when a committed move's responses are lost.

## Rendering and reliability

- Handle GPU allocation and readback failures without reusing stale frame identities.
- Cache orthogonal LCD sampling work and share raw preview pixels without copying the frame.
- Preserve source aspect ratios and scale mixed preview demands consistently.
- Skip Bubble Garden shading outside visible bubbles.
- Update the zstd packages for RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403, and RUSTSEC-2026-0410.

## Upgrade notes

Install the 0.8.0 UI and daemon together. Studio's live saves depend on the scene-write contract introduced in this release.

Scene ETags now contain both the daemon run and revision (`"<run_epoch>:<revision>"`). Preserve the complete ETag in `If-Match`. Numeric revision-only fences remain accepted for older clients, but do not protect against daemon restarts.

Remote transport adapters must accept `Idempotency-Key` and preserve the `hypercolor-run-epoch`, `ETag`, and `Idempotency-Replayed` response headers.

The Python client adds `scene_fence(document)` and `HypercolorPreconditionError.current_fence`. Client 0.7.3 cannot extract `current_revision` from the new 412 response; update clients that depend on this field. Home Assistant currently pins `hypercolor>=0.7.0,<0.8.0`, so its dependency range needs updating before it can adopt the 0.8.0 client.

## Known limitation

Opt-in GPU pass timings currently expose only the last compositor's counters. Scene and display timing aggregation remains a follow-up; frame rendering is unaffected by this diagnostic issue.
